IN.name: India
soil_testing_guidance: Check whether you already hold a Soil Health Card (SHC) at soilhealth.dac.gov.in using your registration number or mobile; if so, enter its values in AgriN.

If not, ask your nearest Krishi Vigyan Kendra (KVK), Block Agriculture Office or state soil-testing laboratory to collect a sample under the Soil Health Card scheme (free for farmers, issued in cycles).
Sample 15-20 cm deep from 8-10 spots across the plot (zig-zag), mix, and submit ~500 g. Record the GPS of each sampling spot in AgriN.
Village-level entrepreneurs and Agri-clinics under the state agriculture department can also run mini soil-test kits.

el_nino.summary: El Nino years tend to weaken and delay the Southwest Monsoon (June-September), raising the odds of below-normal rainfall, longer dry spells and heat stress, especially in central and north-west India.
el_nino.season: Jun-Sep (kharif); carry-over effects on rabi water availability
actions: Prefer short-duration, drought-tolerant varieties
Plan for 1-2 protective irrigations and mulch
Store water (farm ponds, recharge) before the monsoon
Consider crop insurance (PMFBY) before the enrolment deadline

la_nina.summary: La Nina years tend to bring a strong monsoon and, in winter, a colder north India; risk of waterlogging, floods and pest build-up in humid spells.
actions: Ensure field drainage and raised beds
Time harvest windows around forecast rain
Scout more often for fungal disease
Use the surplus rain for groundwater recharge

BR.name: Brazil
soil_testing_guidance: Ask your local EMATER/extension office or a laboratory accredited in the Rede Oficial de Laboratorios de Analise de Solo (ROLAS) for a soil fertility analysis.
Collect 15-20 sub-samples at 0-20 cm depth per homogeneous area, mix and submit ~300-500 g.
Record the GPS of each collection point in AgriN and upload the lab report values.

el_nino.summary: El Nino tends to bring heavier rain and flood risk to southern Brazil and drought/heat to the north and north-east (including the Amazon and Matopiba).
actions: South: improve drainage and adjust sowing windows
North/north-east: drought-tolerant cultivars, soil cover, irrigation planning
Review Seguro Rural / Proagro cover

la_nina.summary: La Nina tends to bring drought and heat to southern Brazil and Argentina-adjacent regions and wetter conditions in the north.
actions: South: water storage, no-till cover, earlier sowing where possible
Diversify planting dates
Review climate insurance

RU.name: Russia

market.name: Ministry of Agriculture - farmer support and markets

soil_testing_guidance: Contact your regional branch of Rosselkhozcentr (agrochemical service) for a soil agrochemical survey.
Take 20 mixed sub-samples from 0-20 cm per field section and record the GPS of each point in AgriN.

el_nino.summary: ENSO influence on Russian agriculture is weaker and indirect; El Nino winters are often milder in parts of the country, with uncertain effects on spring moisture.
actions: Watch winter-crop survival and early spring thaw timing
Keep contingency reserves for spring moisture variability

la_nina.summary: La Nina influence is weak and indirect; can be linked to colder winters and more variable spring moisture in some regions.
actions: Protect winter crops with snow retention
Plan flexible sowing dates

CN.name: China

soil.name: Ministry of Agriculture and Rural Affairs (soil testing & formula fertilization)

soil_testing_guidance: Ask your county agricultural technology extension centre for soil testing and formula-fertilization service (测土配方施肥).
Take 10-15 sub-samples at 0-20 cm per field, mix, submit ~500 g and record GPS of each point in AgriN.

el_nino.summary: El Nino years are often associated with heavier summer rain and flood risk in the Yangtze basin/south and drier conditions in the north.
actions: South: drainage and flood readiness
North: water-saving irrigation and drought-tolerant varieties

la_nina.summary: La Nina years are often associated with drought risk in the south and colder winters in the north.
actions: South: reservoir/irrigation planning
North: protect winter wheat from cold
